target: migrations/053_secondary_street_setback_control_type.sql — add secondary_street_setback to the enforced control_type vocabulary, so the 16 DQ-40 corner-lot rows have somewhere correct to live.
findings_summary: Read the live constraint definition via pg_get_constraintdef on pg_constraint: 'control_type_canonical' is a CHECK over an ARRAY of 21 literals. Enumerated it in full and carried EVERY existing value forward into the replacement — front_setback, side_setback, rear_setback, separation_from_dwelling, privacy_separation, car_parking, bicycle_parking, driveway_width, driveway_gradient, max_site_coverage, max_height, max_floor_area, dwelling_size_min, fencing_height_max, landscaping_min, front_setback_landscaping, deep_soil_min, tree_canopy_min, communal_open_space_min, private_open_space, solar_access_hours — plus the one addition. Confirmed 15 of the 21 are actually in use, so dropping any would risk existing rows; none is dropped. Adding a permitted value cannot invalidate a row, so the ALTER is safe standalone and the migration re-types nothing: the data move is a separate reviewable script. Two other CHECK constraints on the table (applicability, extraction_method) are untouched. Wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT so a failed ADD cannot leave the table with no constraint at all.
